title: RTD
invalidated_by: Any reviewed edit to these entries; bump version.
site_procedure_line: Anything that opens an enclosure or touches the circuit follows your site's lockout procedure with the equipment out of service.

entries.means: A temperature measurement is above its alarm limit.
hypotheses: The measured point really is above its limit, for example after heavy use or because its cooling is not working.

The sensor loop has extra resistance at a lead, terminal, or joint. On most RTD input modules, a fully open loop pegs at the top of the input's range, far above any real temperature — so a believable reading rules out a fully open wire, but not a high-resistance connection or a genuine over-temperature; confirm with a second reading before trusting it.
checks: Read the value and time of each occurrence from the alarm history, and note whether the readings rise after heavy use.

Compare the sensor that does the same work, such as the other side of a left/right pair. If several sensors that share one input alarm together, suspect the shared input; one alone points at that point.

Confirm with a second reading of the same point: its separate over-temperature switch status on the HMI — or, only if your site's procedures let you approach this equipment running and without crossing any guard or barrier, an infrared thermometer read from outside it.

entries.means: A temperature measurement is below its alarm limit.
hypotheses: The measured point really is below its limit.
The RTD or its leads are shorted, or the channel is configured for the wrong sensor type.
checks: Read the actual value and the time of the alarm from the alarm history or the diagnostic view.
Compare the sibling channel at the same location, such as the other sensor of a left/right pair.

Read the input channel's diagnostic (wire break, overrange, underrange) on the HMI diagnostics page or online in the engineering software in view mode only — do not enter configuration or change any setting in the controller.

entries.means: The input channel reports an open circuit in its field wiring.
hypotheses: An open circuit in the field loop: lead, terminal, joint, or the sensor element.
checks: Read the time of the alarm from the alarm history or the diagnostic view.
Compare the sibling channel at the same location, such as the other sensor of a left/right pair.
Read the module and channel diagnostics on the HMI diagnostics page or online in the engineering software in view mode only — do not enter configuration or change any setting in the controller.
does_not_prove: which part of the loop is open
